name: William Floyd
bio: A Delegate and a Representative from New York; born in Brookhaven, Long Island, N.Y., December 17, 1734; pursued an academic course; served in the Revolutionary War, major general in the New York militia; Delegate to the First Continental Congress, 1774; Delegate to the Second Continental Congress, 1775-1776 and 1779-1781; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1781-1783; signed the Declaration of Independence; served in the New York senate, 1777, 1778, and 1784-1788; elected as an Anti-Administration candidate to the First Congress (March 4, 1789-March 3, 1791); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Second Congress in 1790; moved to Westernville, Oneida County in 1794; unsuccessful candidate for New York lieutenant governor in1795; delegate to the New York state constitutional convention in 1801; again a member of the New York state senate, 1808; died on August 4, 1821, in Westernville, N.Y.; interment in Westernville Cemetery, Westernville, N.Y.
